- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days of the forecast, then drifts toward lower values — suggests failure to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward trends after mid-forecast horizon — especially when true values drop below 65.
- Model often fails to capture the “drop-off” after 20–25 days — underestimates the rate of decline or misses the low-range tail (e.g., 50–55 range).
- Model shows persistent lag in recognizing true price corrections — forecasts remain too high even when true values are falling sharply.
- Model exhibits “overconfidence” in early forecast days — forecasts are too optimistic and fail to account for volatility or policy shocks.
- Model does not adjust for “mean reversion” after spikes — tends to hold high values longer than observed in true data.
- Model underestimates the “tail risk” — fails to anticipate sharp drops in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values fall below 55.
